claims.text: A data-driven machine-learning model can rapidly screen the refractory-HEA compositional space.
High-quality experimental and simulation data are available for training such a refractory-HEA model.
Atomic size, mixing enthalpy, density, and thermo-mechanical properties are suitable predictive descriptors for refractory-HEA mechanical performance.
The machine-learning model can capture nonlinear relationships between the selected descriptors and alloy mechanical properties.
Learning these descriptor–property relationships enables the model to identify compositions that reconcile the strength–ductility trade-off.
The model can identify refractory-HEA compositions with reduced density.
Machine-learning-guided alloy selection accelerates refractory-HEA design relative to conventional thermo-kinetic or simulation-based approaches.
Machine-learning-predicted alloys will statistically exhibit a higher strength-to-density ratio than conventionally designed baseline alloys.
Machine-learning-predicted alloys will exhibit improved ductility relative to conventionally designed baseline alloys.
Refractory HEAs are relevant to elevated-temperature structural applications.
Some refractory HEAs retain substantial strength at very high temperatures.
Many refractory HEAs have high density, creating motivation for low-weight composition design.
Model efficacy is limited by the quality and representativeness of the training data.
Predictions are less reliable when extrapolated to underrepresented compositional regimes.
Unmodeled phase-stability effects can reduce prediction reliability.
Conventional thermo-kinetic analysis and simulation methods are time-intensive routes for obtaining refractory-HEA compositions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome expects improvements within model uncertainty bounds, whereas the falsification rule says that improvements falling within those same uncertainty bounds would falsify the hypothesis. Agreement with the predicted uncertainty interval should not by itself constitute falsification.
